https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Andy Burnham promises to be relentless in tackling small boat crossings – video Immigration and asylum Burnham to be ‘relentless’ on small boat crossings after Ceuta crisis Prime minister says UK needs to ‘bring back that control’ and safe routes for refugees are necessary to tackle trafficking Alexandra Topping Political correspondent Sun 2 Aug 2026 14.16 EDT Last modified on Sun 2 Aug 2026 14.38 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Andy Burnham has pledged to be “relentless” in tackling small boat crossings after tens of thousands of migrants entered the Spanish territory of Ceuta, and he said “safe routes” for refugees were necessary to tackle trafficking gangs. Speaking during a visit to Dover, the prime minister said he had been assured by the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, that approximately 98% of the estimated 50,000 people who entered Spain’s north African territory of Ceuta last week had now been returned to Morocco. But while that dealt “substantially” with the immediate issue, “of course there’s a broader issue about the Schengen area and our relationship with it”, he said, adding: “I would want to be in regular dialogue with the EU on those issues”. Asked if he wanted to change the tone of the debate on the issue by stressing the need for safe routes, he said the UK had to “deal with the issue rather than play politics with the issue” and make changes that would reassure the public. “The public don’t like the idea that the border looks like it’s not controlled. We need to bring back that control, but also we need to offer support for people who genuinely need it,” he said. “It’s about changing the whole approach, and slowly but surely we are putting in place those building blocks of a very different approach to this issue.” Last Wednesday was the busiest day for small boat crossings across the Channel so far this year, with 752 people arriving in the UK. Official provisional figures suggest 14,526 have entered the UK so far this year. This is 43% lower than the number recorded by this time last year (25,436) and down 14% on the same period in 2024 (16,903). “Progress is being made but we’re not complacent,” Burnham said. He said the number of National Crime Agency officers tackling organised immigration crime had more than doubled since the start of 2025, from 376 to almost 800. On Sunday the latest figures showed that more than 2,000 people had crossed the Channel in small boats since Burnham became prime minister. Home Office numbers showed 326 people arrived on Saturday in four boats, bringing the number up to 2,057 since he took over from Keir Starmer on 20 July. There were 1,962 crossings in the same period last year. On a separate visit to the National Crime Agency headquarters in Stratford, Shabana Mahmood said the government’s work to tackle small boat crossings were beginning to “bear fruit”. The home secretary has faced fierce opposition within the ranks of the Labour party over proposed immigration measures including doubling the time it takes to qualify for indefinite leave to remain from five to 10 years. But she said reform was needed “to address the pull factors that draw people into boats in the Channel”, adding: “I want to change the calculus. I want them to change their mind about whether they get on the boat in the first place.” She rejected calls to copy Spain’s response to the influx into Ceuta, in which tens of thousands of people have been returned to Morocco without processing any asylum claims. That was possible because Morocco and Spain share a land border and have an agreement in place. Mahmood said people smuggling and the shared waters of the Channel made things “trickier in many ways”. At least 72 people died trying to reach Ceuta, some of them drowning and others being crushed when attempting to climb the border fence. Sánchez called the huge influx “a violation of Spain’s territorial integrity”. The surge of people, which took place over the course of just 24 hours from Thursday, overwhelmed the city of 85,000 people, triggered a political crisis for Madrid and led to an angry reaction from some EU countries, including calls for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen free-movement zone. On Saturday, Spanish police installed a 500-metre (1,640ft) floating barrier off its border ‌with Morocco to prevent others from making their way around the border. But Spain’s leftwing government has continued to come under pressure from right and centre-right governments already angry at its plan to regularise about 500,000 immigrants living in Spain . EU ministers have convened emergency talks for Tuesday . The leaders of 22 EU countries have demanded an emergency response, citing the need to prevent further uncontrolled crossings. The summit was called during a “sobering” meeting of officials representing EU member states and Frontex border agency experts on Saturday, as EU leaders sought to heal divisions in the bloc and restore a unified approach to migration. https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.text: Roberto Vannacci at a National Future news conference in Rome on 5 August. ‘The rest of Europe should sit up and take notice of Mr Vannacci’s rise.’ Photograph: Roberto Monaldo/LaPresse/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Roberto Vannacci at a National Future news conference in Rome on 5 August. ‘The rest of Europe should sit up and take notice of Mr Vannacci’s rise.’ Photograph: Roberto Monaldo/LaPresse/Shutterstock Opinion Europe The Guardian view on Italy’s new far-right party: the rise of a rogue general Editorial The early success of Roberto Vannacci’s National Future sends an ominous signal as extreme politics become normalised Thu 6 Aug 2026 13.29 EDT Last modified on Thu 6 Aug 2026 13.49 EDT Share W hen a serving Italian general published a far-right tract in 2023 entitled The World Turned Upside Down, a disciplinary inquiry swiftly followed. Roberto Vannacci’s text was a sustained exercise in bile and bigotry, attacking among other things the “normalisation” of homosexuality, and questioning whether a high-profile black volleyball star could really be considered Italian. The controversy sent the book into the bestseller charts, and its author was suspended for bringing the army into disrepute. A year out from Italy’s next general election, Mr Vannacci is a problem not for the military but for the country’s prime minister, Giorgia Meloni. Now a member of the European parliament, in February he exploited his notoriety to found National Future, a political party which argues that Ms Meloni’s coalition government has sold out its far-right supporters through not being extreme enough. The “true right”, according to the former paratrooper – who once served as a military attache in Moscow – should be pro-Putin and anti-Ukraine, anti-EU, and committed to restoring the “cultural homogeneity” of Italy through the expulsion of immigrants and their descendants. Shockingly, polls are now placing National Future just behind Forza Italia, the second-biggest party in Ms Meloni’s hard-right coalition, and ahead of its third main component, Matteo Salvini’s League. For Ms Meloni, Mr Vannacci’s rapid rise now threatens to become a major dilemma. To beat the combined forces of the left next year she may require the support of a party that does not disguise its sympathy with Italy’s fascist past. But to seek it would give the lie to efforts to present her own Brothers of Italy party (which retains a neo-fascist political symbol in its logo) as part of the mainstream conservative tradition. The rest of Europe should sit up and take notice of Mr Vannacci’s rise. At a time when Russian influence on the far right is already a cause for concern, he has declared himself open to the idea of funding from Moscow and also Beijing. More broadly, the emergence of National Future confirms that as well as dragging mainstream politics towards more extreme positions on immigration, the continent’s far right is itself radicalising. Here, the equivalent can be found in Rupert Lowe’s Restore Britain party, which has been exerting a rightwards gravitational pull on Reform UK. Poland’s nationalist and Eurosceptic Law and Justice party has embarked on a similar trajectory, in order to compete with two newish and growing far-right parties. In Germany, Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) stands on the brink of a historic breakthrough in state elections in eastern Germany, and leads in national polls. The ominous political consequences were on display last week in the panicked overreaction of leaders to the crisis in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. With one eye over her right shoulder, Ms Meloni was at the forefront of divisive early calls for action to be taken against Spain following an incursion by irregular migrants. For his part, Mr Vannacci used the incident to amplify his calls for a Europe-wide “remigration” strategy. Mr Vannacci’s repugnant politics are beyond the pale. In Germany, the chancellor, Friedrich Merz, continues to rule out any form of national alliance with the AfD. Were Ms Meloni to countenance any form of accommodation with Italy’s rogue general, it would demolish her fragile claims to mainstream respectability. https://www.dw.com/en/congo-m23-rebels-a.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JHEf M23 rebels, backed by Rwanda, have sought to gain control of parts of resource-rich DRC for years Image: Xinhua/picture alliance Advertisement After days of negotiations in Geneva, Switzerland, representatives from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the Rwanda-backed rebel group M23 have agreed to a shared roadmap designed to facilitate peace in the DRC after years of brutal war. The US State Department, which was involved in mediating talks alongside the African Union (AU) , Switzerland and Qatar, released a statement describing the situation on Saturday evening. The State Department said the agreement builds on a US-brokered deal signed last November in Doha, Qatar, adding that Congo and the rebels had "developed a roadmap setting out sequenced steps and timelines for negotiations under the Doha Framework Agreement." Despite a ceasefire being in place since November 15, the shift to peace has been slow, though prisoners, for instance, were recently exchanged. The newly agreed roadmap made clear that an observer mission monitoring the ceasefire will receive support from UN MONUSCO peacekeeping forces and that further negotiations designed to bring about lasting peace will take place soon. How a drone strike on M23 triggered new DRC clashes To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Hundreds of civilians have been killed and millions displaced by fighting between the two sides since early 2022, when M23 — with backing from neighboring Rwanda — began its quest for control of resource-rich eastern Congo and its gold, cassiterite, coltan and diamonds. M23, which is accused of committing brutal wartime atrocities, has controlled large swaths of the North and South Kivu provinces since 2025. The State Department statement released on Saturday said both sides had thanked mediators "for their steadfast support in advancing peace and stability in eastern DRC and the broader Great Lakes region." What does DR Congo gain with the peace deal? https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/23/kill.text: US President Donald Trump and UN Secretary-General António Guterres offered conflicting visions for how the world should manage artificial intelligence at the UN on Tuesday.Armed with a new UN science report that warns of a slight but real potential of catastrophic and irreversible harm, Guterres kicked off the parade of world leaders speaking at the General Assembly by calling for more oversight of AI, warning in vivid if not ominous terms of what could go wrong.“Let us resolve that life-and-death decisions must never be surrendered to machines. Killer robots must have no place in our future,” the UN chief said in his farewell address to world leaders. He also warned about AI in his first General Assembly address a decade ago.With Guterres saying the world needs to “advance the conditions for the responsible pacing of AI and the additional safeguards needed to address risks,” the UN Security Council on Wednesday will address how to place some kind of controls on the technology and it will feature some of the biggest names in the field.It's super, not artificial, Trump says.Less than an hour later, Trump was having none of that.“The United States also totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control for the artificial intelligence being spoken of so much. Now here and after officially called super intelligence, changing the name,” he said.World leaders speaking after Trump used “artificial intelligence” — not “super.”“Every major new technology brings challenges, and superintelligence is no exception," Trump said. “Yet the very same people who said we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming, a name since reborn to climate change, because the planet was cooling, not warming, and nobody was dead.”“These are the same people that are now saying that AI is going to kill us all, that robots are going to attack us, and that everything is going to be a total disaster.”Go slow but cooperate, others sayThe problem is both Trump and Guterres reduce the issue to something that's not useful, says University of Chicago computer science department chairman Henry Hoffmann.“One turns it into a science-fiction movie; the other turns it into a nonissue,” Hoffmann said in an email.“Both push people to pick a team instead of engaging with the real risks and the possible mitigations. There shouldn’t be ‘sides’ on whether we need adequate control over powerful autonomous systems. The interesting debate is over what mechanisms actually provide that control.”Other nations want to make sure they are not left behind during an AI race between the US and China, which Trump said America is winning. French President Emmanuel Macron and Guterres also made the issue about protecting children.“Let’s not wait for the consequences to come raining down on AI," Macron said. "We must act now to protect our children and our young people.”Finland President Alexander Stubb said AI will change the world, potentially for good, but needs strong controls.“Artificial intelligence is the most consequential technology in the history of mankind. It will impact science, the economy, politics, security and the very essence of our humanity," Stubb said.“Humans can and should be in the driver’s seat. We have a choice. We can compete, cooperate or slow down. For me, cooperation is the best way forward.”British Prime Minister Andy Burnham told a meeting of business leaders on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly that he wants to see “a single set of global principles and standards” that can unlock AI’s potential while mitigating its risks.He said forging “AI for good” will be the main focus of the UK’s presidency of the G20 group of nations next year.At Wednesday's Security Council AI meeting, the UN is hearing from the people in building these AI systems, as well as those who have recently sounded the alarm about the need for guardrails.Taking the podium are Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, followed by Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, and finally Clément Delangue, the CEO of and co-founder of Hugging Face, which was hacked by a rogue OpenAI program.

https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/.text: Military Menu Introduction Systems Facilities Agencies Industry Operations Countries Hot Documents News Reports Policy Budget Congress Links WMD Intelligence Homeland Security Space Military Cooperation between the Romanian Armed Force and the US National Guard, enhanced through new joint training projects Romania - Ministry of National Defence Press release No. 187 10.09.2026 On Tuesday, September 8th, the Chief of the Romanian Defence Staff, General Gheorghiță Vlad, met, at the Ministry of National Defence headquarters, with General Thomas M. Carden, the Deputy Chief of the National Guard Bureau of the United States, and Major General David K. Pritchett, the Adjutant General of the Alabama National Guard, who are paying an official visit to Romania. The discussions focused on enhancing cooperation between the Romanian Armed Forces and the US National Guard, with emphasis on the long-standing partnership with the Alabama National Guard, the security situation in the wider Black Sea region, developments in the Euro-Atlantic area, and the implementation of decisions adopted at recent NATO |Summits. The agenda also included identifying new opportunities for joint training and exchange of experience, as well as developing projects that meet current and future security requirements. The experience gained by the Romanian and American troops after having participated in international operations and missions serves as an important benchmark for joint training and increasing interoperability. "The partnership with the Alabama National Guard has grown and strengthened alongside the Romanian Armed Forces. In over three decades of cooperation, we have progressed from exchanges of experience to complex training and projects that directly contribute to our forces' ability to operate jointly. The current security context compels us to look ahead and develop this relationship in areas relevant to collective defence and the strenghtening of the deterrence and defence posture on NATO's Eastern Flank," General Gheorghiță Vlad stated. In his turn, the United States' Ambassador to Romania, Darryl Nirenberg, highlighted the importance of this cooperation for the strategic relationship between the two countries, and noted that "the 33-year partnership between the Alabama National Guard and Romania is a cornerstone of our strategic relationship, which demonstrates the power of long-term defence cooperation. Together, our forces are better prepared to face modern security challenges on NATO's eastern flank." The itinerary of the visit to Romania includes activities in Bucharest, Sibiu and at the "Getica" National Joint Training Center in Cincu. General Thomas M. Carden is scheduled to hold meetings with the commander of the Headquarters Multinational Division South-East and the commander of the Headquarters Multinational Corps South-East. Major General David K. Pritchett will also meet with the chiefs of the Air Force Staff and Land Forces Staff, as well as the commander of the Joint Logistics Command. The Press Office

https://hvg.hu/itthon/20261111_megszunte.text: Nem követett el bűncselekményt Schneider Flóra, aki a választási kampány idején szeretetüzenetekkel írta át a kormány gyűlöletkeltőnek tartott plakátjait. A rendőrség megszüntette a pedagógus ellen indított büntetőeljárást, miután megállapította, hogy bűncselekmény nem történt. Lezárult a gyűlöletplakátokat átfestő tanítónő ellen indított büntetőeljárás: a rendőrség megszüntette a nyomozást Schneider Flóra ügyében. A Magyar Helsinki Bizottság ügyfele ellen rongálás gyanújával indult eljárás, miután a pedagógus a választási kampány idején szeretet- és elfogadáspárti üzeneteket festett kormányzati plakátokra. A tanítónő egy februári éjszaka festékszóróval írt át több, Ukrajnát és a Tisza Pártot támadó plakátot egy óbudai kerítésfalon. Tudatosan olyan hirdetéseket választott, amelyeket korábban már megrongáltak, és lehetőség szerint a leszakított plakátrészekre festett. Üzeneteivel elsősorban a gyerekek nevében tiltakozott a félelemkeltőnek tartott politikai hirdetések ellen. A plakátokra egyebek mellett olyan feliratokat írt, hogy „Boldog és szabad szeretnék lenni, szeretet, elfogadás, egyenlő jogok”, illetve „Én csak élni szeretnék légyszi… ne gyűlölj, szeress”. A rendőrség tetten érte, majd előállította Schneider Flórát, nyolc órán keresztül tartotta bent, lefoglalta a telefonját, majd rongálással gyanúsította meg. A pedagógus ezt követően fordult a Magyar Helsinki Bizottsághoz. A szervezet ügyvédje, Szekeres Zsolt panaszt nyújtott be a gyanúsítás ellen. Érvelése szerint nem történt rongálás, mivel a bűncselekmény megállapításához tényleges kár okozása szükséges. A rendőrség saját megállapítása szerint is korábban már sérült, illetve részben letépett plakátokra kerültek a feliratok. Ezeket a tulajdonosnak egyébként is le kellett volna cserélnie. A nyomozást végül azzal szüntették meg, hogy bűncselekmény nem történt, továbbá az sem volt bizonyítható, hogy az egyetlen épen maradt plakát átfestése is a tanítónőhöz köthető. A Magyar Helsinki Bizottság szerint az ügy azért is jelentős, mert az elmúlt években több ember ellen indult büntetőeljárás politikai üzenetek plakátokra festése miatt. A szervezet emlékeztetett arra, hogy a Kúria 2022-es jogegységi határozata nyomán a hatóságoknak a plakátfirkálásokat a körülményektől és a kár mértékétől függetlenül bűncselekményként kellett kezelniük. A jogvédő szervezet tájékoztatása szerint az Alkotmánybíróság nemrég alkotmánysértőnek minősítette ezt a kúriai előírást. Schneider Flóra ügyében azonban a rendőrség már ezt megelőzően megszüntette az eljárást. Szekeres Zsolt, a Magyar Helsinki Bizottság ügyvédje üdvözölte a nyomozás megszüntetését, ugyanakkor hangsúlyozta: szerinte az eljárásnak el sem kellett volna indulnia. Úgy fogalmazott: Schneider Flóra alapjogát gyakorolta, amikor véleményt nyilvánított, ráadásul úgy, hogy ezzel senkinek nem okozott kárt. A tetőreklámokat sem lehet mindenhol elhelyezni, az óriásplakátok is eltűnhetnek több helyről is.

https://www.bankingnews.gr/analyseis-ekt.text: Τελευταία Νέα 15:57 Θρίλερ - Συγκλονιστική αποκάλυψη για μυστική συνάντηση ΗΠΑ, Ιράν στη Γερμανία – Αγωνιώδες μήνυμα του Trump σε Khamenei 15:52 Παρουσία Δένδια οι Εορταστικές Εκδηλώσεις για την Ημέρα των Ενόπλων Δυνάμεων 15:50 Έντονη ιρανική δράση εναντίον πλοίων στα Στενά του Hormuz – Πλήττεται ο ναυτικός αποκλεισμός των ΗΠΑ 15:41 Δημητροκάλλης για την Ημέρα Ενόπλων Δυνάμεων: Τιμή σε όσους υπηρετούν την Πατρίδα με πίστη, αυταπάρνηση και αφοσίωση 15:27 Εμπλοκή - Οι ΗΠΑ ζητούν γραπτώς από το Ιράν να τερματίσει τον εμπλουτισμό ουρανίου 15:27 Μητσοτάκης: Ο ελληνικός τουρισμός πηγαίνει από ρεκόρ σε ρεκόρ - Αναμένουμε και το 2026 να είναι μία ακόμα εμβληματική χρονιά 15:26 Οικονομικό σοκ - Μαζικός θάνατος μικρομεσαίων επιχειρήσεων από πιστωτική ασφυξία – Έκρηξη 1.604% στα λουκέτα το Νοέμβριο 15:25 Χάος σε Κίεβο, Dnipro – Οι Ρώσοι εντόπισαν Γάλλους κομάντος στην Οδησσό - Le Figaro: Ο Zelensky τρέμει την Le Pen 14:59 Iran proposes 2-day peace plan amid explosions as Houthis strike Saudi Arabia's Shuqaiq and Jizan 14:59 Αδιανόητη δήλωση του Γερμανού ΥΠΕΣ: «Ευχαριστώ GTA 6, κράτησες τους διαδηλωτές μέσα στα σπίτια τους!» Αναλύσεις – Εκθέσεις Σάββατο 07/11/2026 - 14:50 Panic crisis in Europe as US and Russia forge security architecture without EU Russia Ukraine EU Europe NATO security architecture security Germany Brussels Donald Trump Vladimir Putin Volodymyr Zelensky Kaja Kallas Ursula Von der Leyen Friedrich Merz tags : Donald Trump heralds a mammoth deal with Moscow in the absence of Brussels and Kyiv, the return of great power diplomacy, the role of Ukraine, and what is at stake for European sovereignty European capitals find themselves in a state of total diplomatic isolation and absolute panic, watching US President Donald Trump shape the next day of the European security architecture directly with the Kremlin , reducing the European Union to a mere spectator of developments. The tip of the spear is the war in Ukraine , as the Ukrainian front enters a phase of rapid geopolitical ferment, with Washington taking the initiative in moves and preparing a broad security architecture, provoking awkwardness and hysteria among its European allies and within the regime in Kyiv . A major, sensational deal that will thrill everyone! US President Donald Trump announced that he is conducting continuous telephone contacts with Moscow and Kyiv , maintaining that for the first time a reciprocal willingness to achieve a viable solution is evident. In the aftermath of his meeting at the White House with Special Envoy Kirill Dmitriev , the American leader spoke of a «big deal» that will extend beyond the boundaries of Ukraine and will concern the whole of Europe . Concurrently, Jared Kushner revealed that the American side (headed by himself and Steven Witkoff ) is drafting a new framework for stability and security in Europe , which bypasses traditional mechanisms of NATO and imposes direct consultations between Washington , Moscow , and Kyiv . The new framework envisions: regular consultations, military data exchange mechanisms, and deterrence mechanisms along with measures to prevent new conflicts, taking Russian concerns into consideration, effectively nullifying the absolute sovereignty of Brussels in decision-making over the security of its own continent. Indeed, they have already conducted initial contacts in Brussels with representatives of NATO , France , Germany , and Britain . Hysteria in Brussels These announcements sparked a wave of backlash in European capitals. A report in the Financial Times reveals that European officials were taken by surprise by the proposals of Jared Kushner , voicing fears that a direct agreement between Washington and Moscow will marginalize Europe and weaken the standing of NATO . The High Representative of the EU , Kaja Kallas , made it clear that Brussels will not negotiate a new security architecture outside the existing framework of the Atlantic Alliance, stressing that no peace agreement can be implemented without European participation. At the same time, Washington pointedly ignores her appeals. Along the same lines, the Chancellor of Germany , Friedrich Merz , attempted to intervene and, during a telephone call with Donald Trump , underlined that any decision requires the consent of all NATO partners, confirming nevertheless that German diplomacy finds itself completely powerless to influence events. The reaction of European institutions naturally captures the scale of the impasse. Fury in Kyiv... There will be no second Yalta In a state of fury and panic, the Ukrainian leadership, confronted with the prospect of a broader agreement between the great powers, rejects any notion of a diplomatic settlement that takes geopolitical realities into account. For his part, Volodymyr Zelensky , speaking to CNN , characterized the prospect of a broader agreement before a cessation of hostilities on the ground as «dangerous», demanding written and explicit security guarantees from Western allies. The Foreign Minister of Ukraine , Andrii Sybiha , unleashed a fierce attack against the diplomatic initiatives, stating that the future security architecture must not be based on talks with Russia regarding spheres of influence. He argued that European security requires protection from Russia rather than negotiations with it over dividing influence, asserting that there will be no second Yalta and demanding a demonstration of European power instead of half-measures. Russia to Europe: You will participate, but... later, toward the end! Exclusion from Abu Dhabi as well Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov , in public remarks, left open the possibility of European participation at a later stage in the talks, while stressing that Vladimir Putin has approved holding the new round of trilateral negotiations ( Russia , US , Ukraine ) for November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi , where the European side remains excluded from the decisive negotiations while the Russian delegation under Vladimir Medinsky meets with American and Ukrainian officials. Kyiv enters these talks from a position of absolute weakness, desperately seeking an «energy truce», an issue it will raise first, to prevent the total collapse of its infrastructure, security in the Black Sea , as well as preparations for a potential summit meeting. European leaders do not even have a seat at the consultation table. This posture confirms that both Kyiv and its allies in Brussels realize they are being transformed from regulatory actors into mere pawns in a broader geopolitical settlement between the two great powers. Great power diplomacy returns and Europe is missing The issue runs far deeper than the prospect of a peace agreement for Ukraine . It touches upon the way European security will be organized over the coming decades, the relationship between the US and Russia , the cohesion of NATO , and ultimately the standing of Europe in the international system. Hence, the critical question is different: Who will determine the fundamental terms of the agreement, and who will merely be called upon to accept them? This distinction lies at the core of European panic, and not without reason. 1. What «new security architecture» actually means A security architecture is not merely a non-aggression pact or a border settlement. It is the totality of institutions, military balances, international commitments, and deterrence mechanisms that determine: Who guarantees the security of each European state. Where military forces and weapons systems may be stationed. How threats and border violations are addressed. Which states may join military alliances. How a clash between nuclear powers is prevented. Today European architecture was built incrementally after World War II, evolved after 1991 , and rests on institutions such as NATO , the EU , and the OSCE . A key element is the principle that every sovereign state has the right to choose its alliances. Russia has challenged for years the way this principle was applied after the eastward expansion of NATO . Conversely, Eastern European states argue that joining NATO represented an exercise of their sovereignty and a response to historical concerns regarding Russian power. Therefore, a new security architecture could mean two different things: First: Revision and reinforcement of the existing system through new arms control agreements, military transparency, and crisis management. Second: Renegotiation of geopolitical balances, with informal or formal recognition of areas where certain major powers would gain special influence. The difference is fundamental. In the first case, an attempt is made to establish rules of common security. In the second, the security of smaller states risks becoming a bargaining chip between stronger ones. 2. Why Russia seeks a comprehensive agreement and not just an end to the war To understand Russian strategy, one must return to December 2021 . A few months before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine , Moscow presented two draft security treaties to the US and NATO . Its proposals included, among other things: Ending further expansion of NATO . Barring the accession of Ukraine to the Alliance. Restrictions on the deployment of military forces and weapons systems in Eastern Europe . New mechanisms of mutual security guarantees. Of particular significance was the Russian objective to return certain military arrangements to the status quo prior to the 1997 expansion of NATO . This would not necessarily mean countries leaving NATO , but it could entail substantial limitations on the military presence of the Alliance in its eastern wing. The interesting element is that this objective re-emerges in the current diplomatic environment. According to the analysis by Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty on November 6 , Kremlin foreign policy advisor Yuri Ushakov has revived the issue of the military posture of NATO prior to 1997 . The strategic dimension Russia seeks to be treated not solely as a belligerent party in Ukraine , but as a power with which the US must negotiate the security rules for the entire European continent. This carries three potential consequences. First, an upgrade of the diplomatic standing of Moscow . Russia shifts negotiations from the question «how will the war end?» to the question «which security system will replace the post-Cold War order?». Second, linking the Ukrainian issue to broader trade-offs. An agreement could encompass sanctions issues, military deployments, arms control, and future relations between Russia and the West. Third, seeking recognition of special Russian security interests. Here lies one of the most controversial points. Recognizing that Russia has legitimate security concerns is not equivalent to recognizing a right to curb the sovereignty of neighboring states. This constitutes the primary disagreement between the Russian approach and the positions of most European governments. 3. Why the US discusses the whole of Europe with Russia Here we must examine the strategic logic of Washington beyond the Ukrainian front. The US faces an international landscape where its strategic attention is distributed across three major geopolitical theaters: Europe , the Indo-Pacific, and the Middle East . China represents the primary long-term competitor of the US in the Indo-Pacific, while Russia remains a major nuclear power and a fundamental factor in European security. From this perspective, a more stable relationship with Moscow could serve multiple American objectives. A. Reducing the risk of direct clash between NATO and Russia An agreement on military transparency, communication, and arms control could mitigate the danger of inadvertent escalation. This gains particular importance when two nuclear powers are in prolonged confrontation. B. Shifting a greater defense burden onto Europeans A likely American objective is for Europe to assume a larger share of its conventional defense, enabling the US to direct more resources to the Indo-Pacific. This does not necessarily imply abandoning NATO . It could, however, alter the distribution of obligations within the Alliance. C. Managing the Russia-China relationship This is perhaps the most intriguing level of analysis. The deepening strategic partnership between Moscow and Beijing poses a complex dilemma for Washington . An American rapprochement with Russia could theoretically aim to reduce the dependence of Moscow on China . It recalls, in terms of strategic logic rather than an identical historical circumstance, the triangular diplomacy of the US during the 1970s. At that time, the opening between Washington and Beijing exploited the Sino-Soviet split. Today, however, conditions are different. Russia and China have developed extensive energy, economic, and strategic cooperation, sharing the goal of curbing American unipolar influence. Consequently, there is insufficient evidence to assert that a US -Russia agreement could on its own detach Russia from China . 4. The true stakes: Are we returning to the logic of Yalta? Reference to Yalta is inevitable, but caution is warranted. In 1945 the major Allied powers negotiated fundamental aspects of the post-war order. The subsequent division of Europe was tied to the distribution of military power and the emergence of rival blocs. Today we have no confirmed agreement of a similar nature. Yet the comparison gains analytical relevance if the US and Russia begin negotiating: The future military presence of NATO in Eastern Europe . Restrictions on the defense options of Ukraine . The geopolitical position of states situated between Russia and NATO . Acceptance of specific military balances without the consent of those directly concerned. In such a case, a model of security management would emerge in which major powers play a privileged role in establishing rules. This could be interpreted as a return of elements of spheres-of-influence politics. Yet an essential difference from 1945 exists. Modern Europe possesses institutions, economic power, military capabilities, and states with enshrined international sovereignty. It is not a unified, passive geopolitical space. Therefore, an agreement between Washington and Moscow could not automatically bind European states on matters requiring their own consent. This is precisely what Kaja Kallas underlined on November 6 , pointing out that any agreement meant to be implemented will require the participation of the EU . 5. Why Europe is absent... Beyond the fact that this new settlement directly concerns Europe , a structural defect in European security is laid bare here. The European Union is an economic and political power, but lacks a fully unified military command and a single foreign policy across all critical matters. The collective defense of many member states continues to rely on NATO and, by extension, to a significant degree on American military capabilities. This creates an asymmetry. Europe has a direct stake in the security of the continent, it is about its states after all, but Washington commands the military instruments enabling it to exert a decisive influence over relevant negotiations. On the other hand, the US cannot decide alone on European sanctions, on the accession of Ukraine to the EU , or on commitments made by European governments. The reaction of Warsaw On November 6 , Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski laid out a different sequence: First a ceasefire, subsequently negotiations for lasting peace, and only then discussions on reshaping the European security architecture. This stance reflects concern that talks on a comprehensive agreement could take precedence over addressing the war in Ukraine substantively. The position of Moscow The Russian reaction also presents points of interest. On November 6 , Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov acknowledged that discussions on future European security will require AT SOME POINT (not now, not from the outset) the participation of Europeans.
